title: Lamb Tagine
subtitle: Slow-braised Moroccan lamb with apricots and spices
excerpt: Lamb shoulder slow-cooked with dried apricots, cumin, cinnamon, and coriander until deeply tender. Served over couscous with toasted almonds and fresh coriander.

recipe.sourceNotes: A tagine is both the name of a Moroccan slow-cooked stew and the conical clay pot it is traditionally cooked in. The distinctive combination of meat, dried fruit, and warm spices in Moroccan cooking reflects the influence of ancient spice trade routes across North Africa. Lamb with preserved lemon, apricots, and ras el hanout is one of the most celebrated combinations. A heavy casserole or Dutch oven works as well as a tagine for home cooking.

recipeTools.notes: Or a heavy casserole dish with a lid.

content.text: Brown the lamb before braising: this adds flavour that slow cooking alone does not provide. Add the dried apricots for the last hour only, so they soften without completely disintegrating. The tagine should be moist but not soupy: remove the lid for the last 20 minutes to concentrate the sauce if needed.
Heat the oven to 160 C / fan 140 C / gas 3. Heat the oil in a heavy casserole over high heat. Brown the lamb in batches on all sides. Set aside.

In the same pot, fry the onion over medium heat for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and all the ground spices. Cook for 1 minute. Return the lamb. Add the tinned tomatoes, stock, and honey. Season. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook in the oven for 1 hour. Add the apricots. Cover and cook for a further 30 to 40 minutes until the lamb is completely tender. Serve over couscous with fresh coriander.
